title: Database Models and Schemas knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed in the syllabus coverage for “Database Models and Schemas”?
options: Separating database models from API schemas
questions.explanation: The attached FastAPI syllabus lists “Defining database models” under this lesson. The remaining syllabus subtopics are preserved in the lesson file for complete coverage.

questions.prompt: According to the worked example in “Database Models and Schemas”, which result should the learner verify?
options: POST /products with {"name":"Notebook","price":2.5} returns validated JSON; price <= 0 is rejected.
The app publishes itself to production and passes all tests automatically.
HTTP 500 is returned for every valid request.
Input validation and authorization are disabled by design.
questions.answer_key: POST /products with {"name":"Notebook","price":2.5} returns validated JSON; price <= 0 is rejected.
questions.explanation: The worked example explicitly documents this expected result. Reproduce it locally in the listed environment before treating it as tested behavior.

questions.prompt: Which database practice is strongest for this lesson? (Database Models and Schemas)
options: Use constraints, parameterized queries and clear transaction boundaries; verify changes on synthetic test data
Concatenate raw user input into SQL statements
Assume schema auto-generation is always safe to apply in production
questions.answer_key: Use constraints, parameterized queries and clear transaction boundaries; verify changes on synthetic test data
questions.explanation: Data integrity and safe transactions need explicit boundaries and targeted failure tests.
